strategy:
1. Approach and rationale
Use a derivative-free, constrained Differential Evolution (DE) search over complete n-entry sequences. Maintain a population of feasible constructions, generate trial sequences by population-difference mutation and binomial crossover, restore the box and mass constraints by projection, and rank every feasible trial using the exact finite-lag evaluator score. Use per-individual adaptation of the mutation and crossover rates, parent-centered initial perturbations when a parent is available, and bounded stagnation restarts that retain the best candidates.

This is materially different from the earlier proposed smooth log-sum-exp/SLSQP approach, active-gradient search with annealed shakes, pairwise exact line searches, and trust-region LP method. The proposed program uses none of their gradients, epigraphs, nonlinear solvers, pair-coordinate minimizations, or LP subproblems. It searches by recombining whole feasible sequences and evaluating the original nonsmooth objective directly. The exact facts are that the objective is a maximum of finitely many quadratic lag terms and the feasible set is a capped simplex. The hypothesis is that population diversity and restarts may explore basins that a local active-lag or coordinate method misses; they do not guarantee a better score, the requested target, or a global optimum. Projection can also reduce variation when many entries hit box limits, and DE can be costly or stagnate in higher dimensions. Keep the supplied parent as a separate validated fallback so these heuristics cannot force a worse return.

2. Mathematical specification
For runtime length n, use h in R^n, indexed i=0,...,n-1, dx=2.0/n, and required mass S=n/2. The continuous integral constraint corresponds to dx*sum_i h[i]=1. The feasible set is K={h: 0<=h[i]<=1 for every i and sum_i h[i]=S}. Keep the parent resolution when its one-dimensional shape is usable; do not interpolate or change it.

The authoritative score to minimize is C(h)=max(np.correlate(h,1-h,mode='full')*dx). The correlation has M=2n-1 entries and uses finite support, not circular wraparound. Equivalently, its terms are q0=dx*sum_{i=0}^{n-1} h[i]*(1-h[i]) and, for d=1,...,n-1, q[d,+]=dx*sum_{i=0}^{n-d-1} h[i+d]*(1-h[i]) and q[d,-]=dx*sum_{i=0}^{n-d-1} h[i]*(1-h[i+d]). Thus C(h) is the maximum of q0 and both orientations for every positive shift. The shortened sums at nonzero shifts are the boundary terms; do not replace them with full-mass, circular-correlation, or autocorrelation identities. The implementation must nevertheless compute the reported score with the exact np.correlate expression, not a separately accumulated q array.

The search has no smooth surrogate or relaxation: every scored trial is ranked by C(h). The objective is generally nonconvex because of products of h entries and nonsmooth because it is a maximum. DE mutation uses feasible population differences: for feasible x_a and x_b, sum(x_a-x_b)=0. Binomial crossover generally breaks that equality, so project every crossed trial back onto K before scoring.

The joint feasibility projection is the Euclidean capped-simplex projection. For finite v, solve min_h 0.5*||h-v||_2^2 subject to h in K. The scalar KKT multiplier lambda gives h[i]=clip(v[i]-lambda,0,1), where lambda is chosen so sum_i h[i]=S. This is a one-dimensional monotone root problem and is not equivalent to clipping followed by rescaling.

For feasible h, reversal h[::-1] and complement 1-h preserve K. Reversal reverses or permutes the full cross-correlation lag sequence; complement swaps its two correlation operands and reverses that sequence. Their full-lag maximum is therefore unchanged. They may be included as diverse initial population members, but they are not treated as improvements without exact scoring.

3. Implementation procedure
1) Write a top-level run(seed=42, **kwargs) and put every helper at module top level. Use NumPy and math; SciPy and CVXPY are unnecessary. Do not use nested function definitions, closures, lambdas, filesystem or network I/O, or parallel workers. Use the single available CPU sequentially. Do not redefine, serialize, hard-code, or mutate initial_h_values; read it from the runtime global and make local copies when a candidate must be stored.

2) Determine n and the parent. Read the optional global with globals().get('initial_h_values', None), convert it to a float64 array inside exception handling, and regard it as dimensionally usable only if it is one-dimensional with length at least 2. A usable shape sets n to that length and takes precedence over kwargs['n_points'], even when parent entries are nonfinite. Use finite entries as a parent candidate; do not score a nonfinite parent. If no usable shape exists, accept kwargs['n_points'] only when it is a finite integer-valued, non-boolean value in [2,512]; otherwise set n=42. Never resample a usable parent. Convert seed to int for np.random.default_rng; if conversion fails, use 42. Ignore other kwargs.

3) Implement a top-level feasibility predicate is_feasible(h,n). Require a float-convertible one-dimensional vector of length n, finite entries, exact bounds 0<=h[i]<=1, and both abs(np.sum(h)-S)<=1e-10 and abs(math.fsum(float(x) for x in h)-S)<=1e-10. The equality is enforced mathematically by projection; the two small tolerances account only for float64 summation. Aim for mass error at most 1e-12 during correction. Implement a top-level project_capped_simplex(v,n) returning a feasible float64 vector or failure. Reject a wrong shape or nonfinite v. To protect bisection arithmetic, first clip finite input values to [-1e6,1e6]; projection then operates on this bounded input.

   Set lo=min(v)-1 and hi=max(v). At lo, clip(v-lo,0,1) is all ones; at hi it is all zeros. Perform 80 bisection iterations. At midpoint mid, form h=clip(v-mid,0,1); if np.sum(h)>S set lo=mid, otherwise set hi=mid. Form h once more using (lo+hi)/2. Correct any residual without crossing bounds: compute S-math.fsum(h); for a positive residual, scan coordinates and add at most 1-h[i], and for a negative residual subtract at most h[i]. Recompute the residual after each change and stop when its magnitude is at most 1e-12 or no representable change is possible. Repeat a correction using S-np.sum(h) if needed. Finally try setting an interior coordinate j to S minus the stable sum of the other coordinates when that value is in [0,1]. Return the vector only if is_feasible passes; otherwise report failure. Never repair by sequential clipping and rescaling.

4) Implement a top-level exact_score(h,n). Before scoring, require is_feasible(h,n). Compute dx=2.0/n, corr=np.correlate(h,1.0-h,mode='full'), and score=float(np.max(corr*dx)). Return failure for an exception or nonfinite score. This exact helper is the only source of fitness values, candidate comparisons, and the returned c5_bound. It includes all 2n-1 lags and both directions.

5) Establish fallbacks before population construction or search. Create constant_h=np.full(n,0.5,dtype=np.float64), validate it, and compute its exact score. If the finite parent is already in the box and both mass sums differ from S by at most 1e-12, copy it unchanged as parent_seed. Otherwise pass a finite parent through project_capped_simplex; if projection succeeds, store the repaired result as parent_seed. Keep parent_seed and its exact score separately as the parent-derived fallback throughout run. Initialize the global incumbent from parent_seed when available, otherwise constant_h; compare constant_h by exact score and replace only for a strict decrease greater than 1e-12. The original parent is never overwritten.

6) For n<=128, build a deterministic but seeded population. Set P=min(64,max(24,2*n)). A top-level add_unique helper should accept only feasible candidates and reject a candidate if its maximum coordinate difference from any existing member is below 1e-10. Insert parent_seed first when present and unchanged. Then algorithmically construct and add constant_h; a block vector with floor(n/2) leading ones, zeros elsewhere, and a 0.5 at the next coordinate if n is odd; an alternating 1/0 vector from index parity; and the sinusoid 0.5+0.45*sin(2*pi*i/n) for i=0,...,n-1. Project every generated candidate other than an already validated parent copy.

   If parent_seed exists, also try its reversal, complement, and reversed complement through the projection helper. Add up to min(12,P//2) centered Gaussian perturbations: for each, draw z from a standard normal vector, subtract mean(z) from every entry, use sigma values 0.04, 0.10, 0.22, 0.40 cyclically, and project parent_seed+sigma*z. Fill remaining slots with projected independent uniform [0,1] vectors. Without a parent, fill after the four deterministic patterns with projected uniform vectors. Limit unique-candidate attempts to 20*P; if that still gives fewer than P entries, fill remaining slots with copies of existing feasible entries so array dimensions remain P by n. Score every population member with exact_score and compare it against the global incumbent. Keep the parent as the first member when available.

7) Implement synchronous DE generations: every trial in a generation is created from the same old population X of shape (P,n) and old fitness array. Store an F value and CR value per individual; initialize F independently in [0.5,0.8] and CR=0.8. For each target i, copy F[i] and CR[i] to trial parameters. Independently with probability 0.1 replace trial F by 0.1+0.8*U; independently with probability 0.1 replace trial CR by U, where U is a fresh uniform random value. Adopt trial parameters only when the corresponding trial replaces that individual.

   Use two mutation strategies. With probability 0.75 use rand/1: choose distinct r1,r2,r3, all different from i, and set mutant=X[r1]+F_trial*(X[r2]-X[r3]). With probability 0.25 use current-to-pbest/1: sort the old fitnesses, choose p uniformly from the best ceil(0.2*P) indices while excluding i when possible, choose distinct r1,r2 different from i and p, and set mutant=X[i]+F_trial*(X[p]-X[i])+F_trial*(X[r1]-X[r2]). P>=24 guarantees enough distinct indices. These formulas keep the mutant's total mass at S before crossover, up to roundoff.

   Make a binomial trial by choosing each coordinate from mutant with probability CR_trial and otherwise from X[i], then force one uniformly selected coordinate to come from mutant. Project the resulting vector jointly with project_capped_simplex. Reject it if projection fails, it is nonfinite, it fails is_feasible, or its maximum coordinate difference from X[i] is below 1e-14. Otherwise compute exact_score. Never use a mutation model, parameter, or projection residual as a score.

8) Use exact-score selection. Update the global incumbent whenever a validated trial has score less than incumbent_score-1e-12, storing a copy and its exact score. Replace target i in the next population if trial_score<fitness[i]-1e-12. To retain occasional diversity on flat plateaus, also allow replacement when abs(trial_score-fitness[i])<=1e-12, the trial differs from X[i] by at least 1e-6 in maximum norm, and a fresh uniform draw is below 0.02. A tie replacement changes only the population member and its F/CR; it must not displace the global incumbent unless it independently beats it by more than 1e-12. If neither condition holds, retain the old member and parameters. Finish all P trials before replacing X and fitness, so trial creation is synchronous.

9) Use fixed finite search and explicit stagnation restarts. Set max_generations=180 for n<=64 and 100 for 65<=n<=128. Track generations since the global incumbent last improved by more than 1e-12. At 30 such generations, if fewer than three restarts have occurred, keep the global incumbent and the best max(2,P//4)-1 distinct current members. Replace the rest with projected proposals: 75 percent are centered Gaussian perturbations of the global incumbent and 25 percent are projected uniform vectors. Use restart perturbation sigma 0.20, 0.10, then 0.05 for restart numbers one, two, and three. Recompute their exact scores, reset all F values to independent draws in [0.5,0.8], reset CR to 0.8, and reset the stagnation counter. If three restarts have occurred and the global score has not improved for 40 more generations, stop early. Otherwise stop at max_generations. The global incumbent and parent fallback remain stored separately during every restart. A restart-generation exception or a failure to create a proposal leaves the best validated candidate unchanged.

10) When n>128, skip DE to bound single-CPU cost and preserve the original resolution. Still compare by exact_score every available validated parent_seed, constant_h, block pattern, alternating pattern, and sinusoid; do not return an unscored or infeasible pattern. For either search path, wrap population creation and the search loop in exception handling that preserves the already established fallback. Do not use a target threshold as a substitute for exact candidate scoring.

11) Before returning, compare the global incumbent, separate parent-derived fallback when available, and constant fallback using their exact scores, preserving the earlier candidate for differences no greater than 1e-12. Revalidate the selected vector; if it is not feasible, use only project_capped_simplex to repair it and then recompute its exact score. Recompute the score once more for the final unchanged vector. If final validation or scoring fails, return parent_seed if it is valid and scoreable, otherwise constant_h, with its recomputed exact score. Return exactly (h_values, c5_bound, n_points), where h_values is a float64 NumPy array of length n, c5_bound is a Python float from exact_score, and n_points is int(n).

4. Search choices and useful variations
Use the defaults in section 3 without preliminary experiments: parent length fixes n; otherwise use valid kwargs n_points in [2,512] or default n=42; use DE only through n=128; P=min(64,max(24,2*n)); use 180 generations through n=64 and 100 through n=128; allow three restarts after 30 stagnant generations, with the stated final stopping rule. The supplied 42-point construction therefore receives the full population search at its original resolution.

The default mutation mixture is 75 percent rand/1 and 25 percent current-to-pbest/1, with pbest drawn from the best 20 percent. Use per-individual F in [0.1,0.9], CR in [0,1], adaptation probability 0.1, and the stated parent perturbation and restart scales. These are heuristics. A coder may statically select P between 40 and 80, 120-240 generations for n<=64, 70-150 generations for 65<=n<=128, or two to four restarts; pbest fractions between 0.15 and 0.30 and local perturbation scales between 0.03 and 0.45 are also reasonable. Keep the specified defaults when no runtime evidence is available. Any result-dependent restart or termination must follow the explicit in-program rules, not an instruction to measure or tune externally.

Correctness requirements are not tuning options: use the full finite-support np.correlate score, retain both lag directions and boundary truncation, use the runtime parent length without resampling, maintain the box and mass constraints jointly, validate each candidate before scoring or retaining it, and retain a validated parent fallback. The population search is stochastic and local in finite time; no parameter choice certifies global optimality or the requested bound.

5. Numerical robustness and memory use
Use float64 throughout and a local np.random.default_rng(seed); do not alter NumPy's global random state. At the common n=42, P=64 means each population matrix is about 21 KiB. At n=128, each is about 64 KiB; current, next, trial, and restart arrays remain well below a few megabytes. The score helper allocates a full correlation vector of length 2n-1. Direct correlation work is O(n^2) per score, so total search work is O(generations*P*n^2); skip DE above n=128. Do not construct dense Hessians, three-dimensional lag tensors, or higher-resolution grids. All work is sequential on the one available CPU.

Reject nonfinite parent candidates, mutations, projected vectors, and scores. Bound projection inputs before bisection, use 80 iterations, and verify both NumPy and stable sums after residual correction. A failed projection, invalid trial, score exception, or search exception must leave the incumbent and fallbacks untouched. Reinitialization can introduce duplicates if necessary; it must not weaken feasibility. The constant 0.5 vector is a valid fallback for every positive n. Fixed generation, restart, and projection limits ensure termination. The method is heuristic and must not be presented as a certificate of a global optimum.

6. Runtime safeguards and return contract
The generated program must perform dimension parsing, parent validation, projection, candidate feasibility checks, exact objective evaluation, DE search, and fallback selection when the harness later calls run(). Check candidate shape and finiteness, exact coordinate bounds, and both mass sums within 1e-10 before retaining a candidate. Implement the authoritative score internally as max(np.correlate(h,1-h,mode='full')*(2.0/n)); do not return a surrogate, a DE fitness proxy, or a score from circular correlation or an incomplete set of lags.

Create and score the constant fallback before the search loop, and retain a validated parent-derived fallback separately whenever possible. Never mutate initial_h_values. Only a feasible, exactly scored trial may change a population member or the global incumbent. Any failure during search must leave a valid fallback available. Revalidate the final vector, repair only with the joint capped-simplex projection, and recompute the exact score from the returned vector. Return only the required three-tuple with matching vector length and n_points; perform no file or network I/O and print no computed result.
